g0.seoTitle: “I’m Bored” Play Cards for Ages 1–5 | Play Before Pixels
g0.seoDescription: Printable play cards for ages 1–5, sorted by age and energy, with a talk line and a safety line on every card. Color and low-ink PDFs.
long: When your child says “I’m bored,” pull a card and play. Most cards use things you already have: pots, socks, boxes and paper.

This edition holds the two youngest age bands, 1–3 and 3–5. Each card shows a starting age and an energy level: calm, medium or wiggly. It lists what you need, prep time and mess, gives short steps, one thing to say while you play, and a safety line. Cards for children under 5 say “With a grown-up.”
A two-page grown-up guide shows how to start in two minutes, with three talk tips and a pantry list. Every card has an easier way, a harder way and a 2-minute tired-grown-up way.

You get plain PDFs: START HERE, color and low-ink, each in US Letter and A4. Every play follows our published safety rules. Digital file in English; nothing is shipped. Personal license for one household.

g0.seoTitle: Play-First Family Kit for Ages 2–5 | Play Before Pixels
g0.seoDescription: Printable family tools for ages 2–5: a picture checklist, helping jobs, together tokens, a family plan and a 30-day play tracker. Fillable PDF.
long: The Play-First Family Kit gives your day a kind shape: jobs first, then play and time together, then screens at their usual spot. Nothing is taken away; there’s just more play.

Little ones get the Play First, Then Screens picture checklist, a helping-jobs chart and a first-then-later Play-First Board. The whole family gets together tokens, screen-spot cards such as “5 more minutes” and “what we do next”, a rules poster and a Family Play & Screen Plan. A 30-day tracker holds plays that need nothing to buy, each with a starting age, easier and harder ways and a 2-minute version.

Tokens are for play and time together, never screen minutes. The screen spot stays the same every day. A two-page grown-up guide covers a 2-minute setup, three talk lines, and printing, laminating and velcro tips. Every play follows our published safety rules.
Color and low-ink files in US Letter and A4, with type-in fields for free Adobe Acrobat Reader. Instant download; nothing ships.

g0.seoTitle: 30 Days of Back-and-Forth: a Written Play-First Program
g0.seoDescription: 30 short lessons by email, 30 easy plays and plain words for tricky moments, plus a printable workbook. For families with children 0–5.
long: A written 30-day program for families with young children, by email with a printable workbook.

Each morning, one short email comes. It has a lesson you can read in about three minutes and one easy play. It also gives you plain words for one tricky moment, like a show that won’t end, “I’m bored” or a long car ride.

Nothing is banned. Screens get a steady spot in the day, with the same time and the same ending. They are never a prize or a punishment. The rest of the day fills up with play and back-and-forth talk.
Every play has a starting age, an easier and a harder version and a 2-minute version for tired days. Every play uses things you already have and follows our published safety rules.
It is parent education, not medical advice. There are no videos, calls or coaching.
